data.narrative:
Sereact, a Series B robotics and manufacturing company founded by Ralf Gulde and Marc Tuscher, has raised $140M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of 3 same-stage, same-sector private peers (Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity) plus 1 public comparable and 5 additional private reference companies.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression method, using total capital raised as a proxy base and applying a 1.9x Series B step-up multiplier, yields $266M. The peer-median approach references the median valuation of $1.8B across the 3-company peer set, with a range of $1.6B to $2.0B. The dispersion between methods reflects meaningful differences in capital efficiency and market positioning relative to identified peers.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $226M (low) to $2.0B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The 9x spread between methods points to two key uncertainties: first, whether Sereact's unit economics and growth trajectory align with capital-efficient stage-progression benchmarks or command peer-set valuations; second, positioning relative to the $1.6B–$2.0B peer band. Resolution of these gaps would require clarity on revenue trajectory, gross margins, and customer concentration versus comparable companies.
